competitive_landscape: The island is served today by high-speed diesel ferry operators (Superdong, Phu Quoc Express) on the Rach Gia and Ha Tien crossings, plus tour-boat operators and the Sun World Hon Thom cable car for the An Thoi islands. The growth is explosive and the spend is premium, but there is no on-demand, no foiling and no zero-emission option — the entire transfer layer is undifferentiated diesel, which is precisely the opening.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Covers the whole island system: Ha Tien crossing (~24 nm), An Thoi/Hon Thom hops (~5–8 nm) and resort transfers all sit comfortably inside 70 nm; the Rach Gia crossing (~64 nm) is a flagship all-electric showcase near the range edge.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Unlocks long mainland and cross-Gulf legs (Phu Quoc↔HCMC/Mekong-delta coast, and potential cross-border links toward the Cambodian Kep/Kampot coast), and — critically for a greenfield island building out faster than its grid — removes any charging-infrastructure dependency via diesel refuel plus quiet-mode electric.

precedents.what: Navier's $100M, ~100-vessel phased network with JIH Global
precedents.why_it_matters: Phu Quoc is structurally the same problem — a branded resort-island archipelago reached by slow boats — so the Maldives network is the directly transferable playbook to replicate here.

regulatory_note: Phu Quoc sits in Kien Giang province and operates an international airport and visa-exemption regime that has fuelled its arrivals boom. As a designated economic and tourism special zone with aggressive green-growth and net-zero-2050 alignment, a zero-emission marine fleet fits national clean-transport policy; cross-Gulf routes toward Cambodia would additionally touch CIQ/maritime-border process.
seasonality: Phu Quoc's dry season (Nov–Apr) is calm and peak; the SW monsoon (May–Oct) brings rain, wind and Gulf swell that roughen the mainland ferry crossings and disrupt tour boats. Foiling's smoother, faster ride and better sea-state tolerance turn the monsoon-shoulder crossings — the worst part of the diesel-ferry experience — into a reliable premium leg.

summary: Phu Quoc is Vietnam's largest island and its hottest resort frontier — JW Marriott, Regent, InterContinental and a wave of new development drew nearly 6 million visitors in 2024, including almost 1 million international arrivals (up ~74%). Yet the mainland link is still a slow diesel ferry (2.5h+ from Rach Gia), and the An Thoi archipelago to the south is a string of islands begging for clean, fast hops. It is structurally a Maldives-style resort-island network — exactly the model Navier is replicating with JIH Global in the Maldives.
tagline: Vietnam's fastest-rising resort island — nearly 6 million visitors a year, still reached by a 2.5-hour mainland ferry. The Maldives playbook, on the Gulf of Thailand.

use_cases.body: Clean, fast foiling between Phu Quoc's south coast, Hon Thom and the An Thoi islands replaces slow tour boats — a premium 'island-hopping' experience for resort guests and day-trippers, with the cable car as one option and on-demand foiling as the upgrade.
